text:
kai: quick thought  for long streaming responses id prefer a trailer-based resume token (http trailers) vs stuffing a big opaque blob in the request header. pros: avoid sending checkpoint payloads to every upstream, smaller client footprint, reduce leakage surface on early retries. cons: requires proxies/support for trailers. thoughts?

maria: trailers are nice for big outputs but not all frontdoors/clients support them (mobile sdk, old proxies). need a clear fallback.

ingrid: agree. suggest a hybrid handshake: client always sends a lightweight `X-RW-Session: v1|sid` header (small uuid). server emits a `Resume-Trailer: v1|base64(...)` as the final trailer with the checkpoint blob. proxies that support trailers forward it; those that don't should translate trailer -> backend-store keyed by sid.

kai: good pattern. for midstream resume the proxy would send `Resume-Start: v1|sid|offset|hmac` to the backend so backend can replay from offset. backend returns `Resume-Ack` or `Resume-Nack` explaining why resume failed (missing checkpoint, stale).

sam.w: security: resume blobs must be hmac-signed and must not include raw user ids. include only last_chunk_index + compact checksum + small proto of model-state hints. ops needs key rotation and migration plan.

maria: also add a per-route policy: `stream.resume = { mode: off | trailers | header_fallback, retention_seconds: int }`. default off for side-effecting flows. trailers preferred for high-throughput generative endpoints.

ingrid: implementation constraints for proxies: 1) low-memory: avoid buffering entire stream to compute trailer; rely on backend to emit trailer and forward it on the fly, 2) on resume, proxy must reconstruct `Resume-Start` including trusted-to-edge metadata, 3) if proxy stores checkpoints in local store for fallback, ensure encryption-at-rest and TTL.

kai: SLO/design goal: resume handshake and warmup should add <200ms median to resumed requests. that implies caching of small state at edge for short TTL. otherwise resume is worse than restart.

sam.w: logging/telemetry: do not log raw resume blob. log only 8-byte trace-hash plus metadata: resume.attempt, resume.origin(client|edge), resume.result(ok|nack|invalid_hmac). sampling bit default 0; ops can enable low-rate sampling for deep debugging.

maria: client semantics: require clients to include `should_resume=true|false`. if false, don't attempt automatic resume on disconnect to avoid double side-effects. also recommend client backoff and jitter.

ingrid: backend contract: on Resume-Start, backend MUST respond quickly with either `Resume-Ack: v1|ok|offset` or `Resume-Nack: v1|reason`. avoid opaque 5xx on resume paths so proxies can decide fallback policy.

kai: compatibility: for proxies lacking trailer support, they translate trailer->store keyed by sid. legacy behavior: no resume. we need a migration matrix.

ops-bot: created RW-5010: "streaming resume handshake compatibility matrix" and notified #eng-oncall.

maria: metrics to monitor during rollout: resume.attempts, resume.latency.p50/p95, resume.success_rate, resume.nack_reasons, resume.store_hits, resume.store_misses, resume.hmac_invalid.

sam.w: also add a canary phase where we enable trailers in a single region with low traffic and compare resume win-rate vs restart penalties.

kai: i'll draft RFC with: handshake state machine, example proto for trailer blob (resume_id, last_chunk_index, small model-state hint), proxy requirements, edge store TTL, kms/hmac policy, route knobs, and rollout checklist. tagging infra/ops/security for key policy. thanks everyone.
